Thank you for your patience. ::: :::: The original files in `_labs/lab3` are below: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fs::dir_tree(path = "_labs/lab3/") ## _labs/lab3/ ## ├── app-api.R ## ├── app-api.py ## ├── eda-db.qmd ## ├── model-db.qmd ## ├── py-data-load.py ## └── r-data-load.R ``` ::: In the previous labs, we build a model API with [`vetiver`](https://rstudio.github.io/vetiver-python/stable/) (also [available in R](https://rstudio.github.io/vetiver-r/)). This lab continues with accessing databases and using APIs. ## APIs Let's back up a bit and get an understanding of what an API does. In general, APIs are the digital plumbing that makes modern software ecosystems possible. ```{mermaid} %%| fig-cap: 'APIs' %%| fig-align: center %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral', 'look': 'handDrawn', 'themeVariables': { 'fontFamily': 'monospace', "fontSize":"16px"}}}%% graph LR DS["Data Scientist"] --> Req["API Request"] Req --> ApiServ["API Server"] ApiServ --> DataProcMod["Data Processing/Model"] DataProcMod --> Res["Results"] Res --> ApiServ ApiServ --> APIResp["API Response"] APIResp --> DS style ApiServ fill:#e1f5fe style DataProcMod fill:#f3e5f5 ``` APIs have standardized language that allows different software systems to communicate and share functionality (without needing to understand how the internal implementation works). **What do they communicate?** 1. What you can request (endpoints) 2. How to make the request (HTTP methods, parameters) 3. What you'll get back (response format) 4. When things go wrong (error codes) In the previous lab we turned our model into a `VetiverModel()`, saved it to a `pins` board, and then created a `VetiverAPI()`: ```{mermaid} %%| fig-cap: 'Our pipeline' %%| fig-align: center %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral', 'look': 'handDrawn', 'themeVariables': { 'fontFamily': 'monospace', "fontSize":"16px"}}}%% graph LR subgraph DataPrep["Data Preparation"] Penguins["penguins
data"] --> DuckDB["put in
duckdb"] DuckDB end subgraph ModTrain["Linear Regression"] DuckDB --> LinReg["create
model"] LinReg end subgraph MLOps["MLOps"] LinReg --> VetMod["create
VetiverModel()"] VetMod --> Pins["save to
pins board"] Pins --> VetAPI["create
VetiverAPI()"] end style ModTrain fill:#e1f5fe style MLOps fill:#f3e5f5 style VetAPI fill:#e8f5e8 ``` I've also completed these steps in R, which can be found in [`_labs/lab2/R/model-vetiver-r.qmd`](https://github.com/mjfrigaard/do4ds-labs/tree/main/_labs/lab2/R/model-vetiver-r.qmd). The sections below cover how to create and communicate with APIs. I've split each lab into separate `R/` and `Python/` folders and included RStudio project files. ## R App API The R App API files can be found in the [`_labs/lab3/` folder](https://github.com/mjfrigaard/do4ds-labs/tree/main/_labs/lab3/). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fs::dir_tree(path = "_labs/lab3/") ## _labs/lab3/ ## ├── app-api.R ## ├── eda-db.qmd ## └── r-data-load.R ``` ::: ### eda-db.qmd {#sec-eda-db.qmd} The [`eda-db.qmd`](_labs/lab3/eda-db.qmd) file has the EDA R code from lab 1. It begins by loading the libraries: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(DBI) # add this library(duckdb) # add this library(palmerpenguins) # add this library(dplyr) library(ggplot2) library(dbplyr) ``` ::: The code below creates a connection to the database, but needs to be changed slightly so the `penguins` data is registered with `duckdb` (before the queries can be run). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # load penguins data first penguins_data <- palmerpenguins::penguins # then connect con <- DBI::dbConnect( duckdb::duckdb(), dbdir = "my-db.duckdb" ) # register table duckdb_register(con, "penguins_data", penguins_data) # create table dbExecute(con, "CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE penguins AS SELECT * FROM penguins_data") # create df df <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM penguins") |> na.omit() ``` ::: The table below displays the means of the measurements (body mass, flipper length, and bill length/depth) by species and sex: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} df %>% group_by(species, sex) %>% summarise( across( ends_with("mm") | ends_with("g"), \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE) ) ) %>% dplyr::collect() %>% knitr::kable() ``` ::: The graph displays the best-fit linear relationship between `bill_length_mm` and `body_mass_g` by `species`: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} df %>% ggplot( aes( x = bill_length_mm, y = body_mass_g, color = species) ) + geom_point() + geom_smooth(method = "lm") ``` ::: And we finish by closing the connection to the database. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} DBI::dbDisconnect(con) ``` ::: To view the original code in `eda-db.qmd`, expand the section below:
Expand to view eda-db.qmd ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ```` --- title: "Penguins EDA" format: html: code-fold: true --- ## *Penguin Size and Mass by Sex and Species* ```{r} library(dplyr) library(ggplot2) library(dbplyr) con <- DBI::dbConnect( duckdb::duckdb(), dbdir = "my-db.duckdb" ) df <- dplyr::tbl(con, "penguins") ``` ```{r} df %>% group_by(species, sex) %>% summarise( across( ends_with("mm") | ends_with("g"), \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE) ) ) %>% dplyr::collect() %>% knitr::kable() ``` ## *Penguin Size vs Mass by Species* ```{r} df %>% ggplot(aes(x = bill_length_mm, y = body_mass_g, color = species)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth(method = "lm") ``` ```{r} DBI::dbDisconnect(con) ``` ```` ::: :::
### app-api.R `app-api.R` creates an R Shiny application that calls the `vetiver` API. The top of the file creates an `api_url`: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} api_url <- "http://127.0.0.1:8080/predict" ``` ::: #### UI The UI definition is below: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ui <- fluidPage( titlePanel("Penguin Mass Predictor"), # Model input values sidebarLayout( sidebarPanel( sliderInput( "bill_length", "Bill Length (mm)", min = 30, max = 60, value = 45, step = 0.1 ), selectInput( "sex", "Sex", c("Male", "Female") ), selectInput( "species", "Species", c("Adelie", "Chinstrap", "Gentoo") ), # Get model predictions actionButton( "predict", "Predict" ) ), mainPanel( h2("Penguin Parameters"), verbatimTextOutput("vals"), h2("Predicted Penguin Mass (g)"), textOutput("pred") ) ) ) ``` ::: #### Server The server definition is below: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} server <- function(input, output) { # Input params vals <- reactive( list( bill_length_mm = input$bill_length, species_Chinstrap = input$species == "Chinstrap", species_Gentoo = input$species == "Gentoo", sex_male = input$sex == "Male" ) ) # Fetch prediction from API pred <- eventReactive( input$predict, httr2::request(api_url) |> httr2::req_body_json(vals()) |> httr2::req_perform() |> httr2::resp_body_json(), ignoreInit = TRUE ) # Render to UI output$pred <- renderText(pred()$predict[[1]]) output$vals <- renderPrint(vals()) } ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server) ``` ::: ### r-data-load.R {#sec-r-data-load-r} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), dbdir = "my-db.duckdb") DBI::dbWriteTable(con, "penguins", palmerpenguins::penguins) DBI::dbDisconnect(con) ``` ::: To view the original code in `r-data-load.R`, expand the section below:
Expand to view r-data-load.R ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), dbdir = "my-db.duckdb") DBI::dbWriteTable(con, "penguins", palmerpenguins::penguins) DBI::dbDisconnect(con) ``` ::: :::
## Python App API The Python App API files can be found in the [`_labs/lab3/Python/` folder](https://github.com/mjfrigaard/do4ds-labs/tree/main/_labs/lab3/Python). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fs::dir_tree(path = "_labs/lab3/Python/") ## _labs/lab3/Python/ ## ├── Python.Rproj ## ├── app-api.py ## ├── model-db.qmd ## └── py-data-load.py ``` ::: ### model-db.qmd The [model-db.qmd](_labs/lab3/model-db.qmd) file contains the EDA from [lab 1](lab1.qmd). ### app-api.py `app-api.py` creates an Python Shiny application that calls the `vetiver` API. ### py-data-load.py
